analysis.title: AI delivers despite volatility (UBS House View - Daily Asia)
key_insights: Nasdaq fell 1.4% on Thursday. Alphabet shares fell 12.3% after most core businesses reported September-quarter sales below market expectations.
Amazon fell 6.9% in after-hours trading after its core e-commerce business grew at the slowest pace in three years. Amazon also reported higher-than-anticipated capital spending.
Cloud revenue growth accelerated at Alphabet and Amazon. Microsoft's Azure exceeded expectations and Oracle beat estimates on both revenue and earnings.

UBS says the reaction reflects elevated expectations going into reporting season and a sharper investor focus on AI monetization. It says results reinforce its view that AI fundamentals remain robust and support a constructive outlook on the AI trade.

Google Cloud revenue grew 103% y/y, up from 82% in the prior quarter and 34% in the March quarter. Azure grew 48% in the September quarter versus 43% in June. Oracle cloud growth rose to 62% from 47%. Amazon's cloud unit accelerated for a sixth straight quarter.
The hyperscalers gave positive outlooks for further cloud growth and said added capacity could support demand in their pipelines.

AI product monetization is showing up: Microsoft reported an eight-fold increase in large Copilot accounts and Alphabet said Gemini reached 1 billion users. A leading AI lab reported compute costs below 60% of revenue and AI spending from its large enterprise customers at under 1% of their total expenses.

Microsoft trimmed 2026 capex guidance from USD 175bn to USD 170bn but said investment will accelerate next year. With Meta's recent equity issuance and Alphabet and Amazon signalling significant 2027 capex increases, UBS expects AI capex growth to stay robust.

UBS raised its aggregate AI capex forecasts to USD 1tr in 2026 and USD 1.4tr in 2027, and introduced a USD 1.5tr forecast for 2028. It says this should benefit quality semiconductor and hardware names.

UBS sees opportunities in hyperscalers and high-quality semiconductor and hardware companies. It advises managing concentrated positions through more defensive tech exposure and diversification across sectors and regions, and suggests structured strategies with capital preservation or yield features for investors who can tolerate the risks.
UBS cautions on funding pressures and execution risks at specialized AI cloud providers, while rising GPU rental prices point to robust compute demand amid supply constraints.

market_movers.rationale: Shares fell 12.3% after most core businesses reported September-quarter sales below market expectations, while Google Cloud revenue grew 103% y/y.
Shares fell 6.9% after hours as core e-commerce grew at its slowest pace in three years and capex came in above expectations. Cloud growth accelerated for a sixth straight quarter.

sector_views.rationale: AI fundamentals remain robust, cloud growth is accelerating and capex is rising. UBS favors hyperscalers and high-quality semiconductor and hardware names, and advises diversifying into more defensive tech areas.

earnings_insights: Alphabet: most core businesses reported September-quarter sales below market expectations (reported), shares fell 12.3% on Thursday. Google Cloud revenue grew 103% y/y (reported), versus 82% in the prior quarter and 34% in the March quarter.
Amazon: core e-commerce grew at its slowest pace in three years (reported), capital spending came in above expectations, and the cloud unit accelerated for the sixth straight quarter.
Microsoft: Azure grew 48% for the three months to September (reported) versus 43% for the June quarter, and exceeded expectations. 2026 capex guidance trimmed from USD 175bn to USD 170bn.
Oracle: beat estimates on both revenue and earnings (reported), cloud growth quickened to 62% from 47%.

trade_ideas.description: Structured strategies with capital preservation or yield-generating features for investors tolerating AI-trade volatility
trade_ideas.rationale: Manage potential volatility while keeping exposure to the AI trade.

risk_factors: Elevated expectations going into reporting season and sharper investor focus on AI monetization.
Funding pressures and execution risks at specialized AI cloud providers.
Overly concentrated positions in AI-linked tech.
vol_and_positioning: Nasdaq fell 1.4% on Thursday on the tech earnings reaction. UBS suggests structured strategies with capital preservation or yield-generating features to manage potential volatility.

tension_points.bull_case: Cloud growth accelerated at Alphabet (103%), Azure (48%), Oracle (62%) and Amazon, with Copilot large accounts up eight-fold and Gemini at 1 billion users, supporting returns on AI investment.
tension_points.bear_case: Alphabet fell 12.3% on core-business sales misses and Amazon fell 6.9% on slow e-commerce growth and higher capex, showing elevated expectations and funding and execution risks at specialized AI cloud providers.

theme_stances.key_argument: Accelerating cloud growth shows hyperscalers can generate returns on AI investment, and capex should keep supporting the compute complex.
theme_stances.evidence: AI fundamentals remain robust overall and support our constructive outlook on the AI trade
